input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.
I just checked my phone, and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure if I can make calls or use the internet right now. What should I do?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, at the top of my screen, it says “No Signal” and something about data being disabled. Is that normal? I still don’t know if I can send a picture message. What should I do next?

I checked, and it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what to do about that—does that mean my SIM card isn’t in properly? I’m a bit nervous about taking it out and putting it back in. Is there an easy way to fix this?

Alright, I went ahead and reinserted the SIM card like you described. Now, at the top of my screen, I see some bars for signal (though it says “Poor”) and something about 2G and data being enabled. Is that better? What should I do next?

I changed the network setting to “4G/5G preferred” like you said, and now my phone shows excellent signal and 5G at the top. But I still can’t send picture messages—it’s still not working. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I did that. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit worried—if I reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I do this?
Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, and I’m getting a bit more anxious about this. Is there anything else we can try?

I checked my phone, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned ON. I’m not using any VPN, and I couldn’t find anything called “Messaging” in my app permissions—maybe it’s called something else? What should I do about the Wi-Fi Calling being on? Should I turn it off?
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working. Should we check the app permissions next? I’m not sure where to find those.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” I don’t see storage or SMS permissions enabled. Should I turn those on? If so, can you walk me through how to do that?

I enabled both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, and I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed. Is there anything else we can try?

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hello, I’m having trouble sending those picture messages—MMS, I think they’re called—from my phone. It’s been a few hours now and nothing seems to go through. Can you help me fix this?

I can help you troubleshoot your MMS (picture messaging) issue. To get started, I’ll need to identify your account. Could you please provide one of the following:

- The phone number associated with your account,
- Your full name and date of birth (YYYY-MM-DD format), or
- Your customer ID (if you have it)?

Once I have this information, I can assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started.

Thank you for providing your information. I have identified your account. To help you fix the MMS (picture messaging) issue, I’ll need to guide you through a few quick checks and steps on your phone.

First, can you confirm if you are able to make regular calls and use mobile data (for example, browsing the web) on your phone right now? This will help determine if the issue is specific to MMS or related to your overall service.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔋 80%
I just checked my phone, and I see a little airplane icon at the top. Does that mean something is wrong? I’m not sure if I can make calls or use the internet right now. What should I do?

The airplane icon means that Airplane Mode is enabled on your phone. When Airplane Mode is on, all wireless connections—including cellular service, calls, mobile data, and MMS—are disabled. This is likely the reason you can’t send picture messages.

Please turn off Airplane Mode on your phone. You can usually do this by:

1. Swiping down from the top of your screen to open the quick settings menu.
2. Tapping the airplane icon to turn it off.

Once Airplane Mode is off, check if you can make calls or send a picture message. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you need further assistance.

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📵 No Signal | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode like you said. Now, at the top of my screen, it says “No Signal” and something about data being disabled. Is that normal? I still don’t know if I can send a picture message. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update. Seeing “No Signal” and data being disabled means your phone is not currently connected to the cellular network, which will prevent you from sending MMS messages.

Let’s try to resolve this step by step:

1. Please check if your SIM card is properly inserted and active. On your phone, look for an option in your settings called “SIM status” or “About phone” > “SIM status.” 
2. If you see any message about the SIM being missing or inactive, try removing the SIM card and reinserting it securely.

After you’ve checked and reseated your SIM card, let me know if the signal returns or if you still see “No Signal.” If you need instructions on how to check or reseat your SIM card, please let me know your phone model and I can guide you further.
No SIM card detected in the phone.

I checked, and it looks like my phone says there’s no SIM card detected. I’m not sure what to do about that—does that mean my SIM card isn’t in properly? I’m a bit nervous about taking it out and putting it back in. Is there an easy way to fix this?

If your phone says there’s no SIM card detected, it usually means the SIM card isn’t inserted properly or has lost contact with the phone’s SIM slot. This is a common issue and can often be fixed by reseating the SIM card.

Here’s what you can do:
1. Power off your phone.
2. Locate the SIM card tray (usually on the side or back of your phone).
3. Use the SIM eject tool (or a small paperclip) to gently open the tray.
4. Remove the SIM card, check for any dust or damage, and then carefully reinsert it.
5. Close the tray and power your phone back on.

If you’re uncomfortable doing this yourself, you can visit a local store for assistance. However, reseating the SIM card is generally safe and straightforward.

Once you’ve done this, check if your phone now detects the SIM card and if you have signal. Let me know what you see after trying these steps, and I’ll guide you further if needed.

SIM card re-seated successfully.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

Alright, I went ahead and reinserted the SIM card like you described. Now, at the top of my screen, I see some bars for signal (though it says “Poor”) and something about 2G and data being enabled. Is that better? What should I do next?

Great job! Now that your phone detects the SIM card and you have some signal, you’re making progress. However, seeing “2G” and “Poor” signal means your phone is connected to an older, slower network, which often isn’t suitable for sending MMS (picture messages).

Let’s improve your connection for MMS:

1. Please go to your phone’s network settings.
2. Look for an option called “Preferred network type” or “Network mode.”
3. Change the setting to “4G/5G preferred” or “4G only” if available.

This will allow your phone to connect to faster networks that support MMS.

After making this change, check if your signal improves and try sending a picture message again. Let me know if you’re able to send MMS now or if you still have issues.

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.

I changed the network setting to “4G/5G preferred” like you said, and now my phone shows excellent signal and 5G at the top. But I still can’t send picture messages—it’s still not working. Is there something else I should try? I’m starting to get a bit frustrated.

Thank you for updating the network settings and letting me know the results. Since you now have excellent signal and 5G, your basic connectivity is good. The next most common reason for MMS issues is incorrect APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for sending picture messages.

Let’s try resetting your APN settings to default:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find “Mobile Network” or “Cellular Network.”
3. Tap on “Access Point Names” or “APN.”
4. Look for an option to “Reset to default” or “Reset settings.”

After resetting the APN settings, please restart (reboot) your phone for the changes to take effect.

Once your phone restarts, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still need help.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%

I found the option to reset the APN settings, and I did that. It says the settings will reset when I restart my phone. But I’m a bit worried—if I reboot my phone, will I lose any of my photos or messages? I really don’t want to lose anything important. Can you reassure me before I do this?

You will not lose any of your photos, messages, or personal data by simply restarting (rebooting) your phone. Restarting your phone only refreshes the system and applies any new settings, such as the APN changes you just made. All your files, apps, and information will remain safe and unchanged.

It’s safe to go ahead and restart your phone now. Once it powers back on, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works or if you need further assistance.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...

Alright, I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, and I’m getting a bit more anxious about this. Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience and for following the previous steps. Since you still can’t send picture messages after confirming your signal, network mode, and APN settings, let’s check a few more things that can affect MMS:

1. Is Wi-Fi Calling enabled on your phone? Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling turned on can interfere with MMS. Please check your phone’s settings for “Wi-Fi Calling” and let me know if it’s enabled.
2. Are you connected to a VPN? If you use a VPN app, try disconnecting it and then attempt to send an MMS.
3. Does your messaging app have the necessary permissions? The app needs permission to access storage and SMS.

Could you please check these settings and let me know:
- If Wi-Fi Calling is ON or OFF,
- If you are using a VPN,
- If your messaging app has storage and SMS permissions enabled.

Once you provide this information, I’ll guide you through the next steps.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned ON.
VPN is turned OFF.
App 'Messaging' not found on this phone.

I checked my phone, and it looks like Wi-Fi Calling is turned ON. I’m not using any VPN, and I couldn’t find anything called “Messaging” in my app permissions—maybe it’s called something else? What should I do about the Wi-Fi Calling being on? Should I turn it off?

Yes, please turn OFF Wi-Fi Calling on your phone. Sometimes, having Wi-Fi Calling enabled can interfere with sending MMS (picture messages).

To do this:
1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Find the “Wi-Fi Calling” option (it may be under “Connections” or “Network & Internet”).
3. Toggle Wi-Fi Calling OFF.

After turning off Wi-Fi Calling, try sending a picture message again. Let me know if this resolves the issue or if you still need further assistance. If it still doesn’t work, we can check your messaging app’s permissions together.

Wi-Fi Calling is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I turned off Wi-Fi Calling like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working. Should we check the app permissions next? I’m not sure where to find those.

Yes, let’s check your messaging app’s permissions next, as missing permissions can prevent MMS from working.

Here’s how you can check and update permissions for your messaging app:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app (it might be called “Messages,” “Messaging,” or something similar).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Make sure that both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions are enabled (allowed).

If either permission is not enabled, please allow it. After updating the permissions, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you need help finding your messaging app or if you’re unsure which app you’re using for text and picture messages.

I checked the permissions for my messaging app, and it looks like it only has permission for “phone.” I don’t see storage or SMS permissions enabled. Should I turn those on? If so, can you walk me through how to do that?

Yes, you should enable both “Storage” and “SMS” permissions for your messaging app. These permissions are necessary for sending and receiving picture messages (MMS).

Here’s how to enable them:

1. Go to your phone’s Settings.
2. Tap on “Apps” or “Applications.”
3. Find and select your messaging app (it may be called “Messages,” “Messaging,” or similar).
4. Tap on “Permissions.”
5. Look for “Storage” and “SMS” in the list.
6. Tap on each one and select “Allow” or “Enable.”

After you enable both permissions, try sending a picture message again.

Let me know if you were able to enable the permissions and if MMS is now working. If you need more detailed steps for your specific phone model, let me know what type of phone you have (e.g., Samsung, Google Pixel, iPhone, etc.).

I enabled both the storage and SMS permissions for my messaging app, but I still can’t send picture messages. It’s still not working, and I’m starting to feel a bit overwhelmed. Is there anything else we can try?

Thank you for your patience and for following all the troubleshooting steps so far. Since you have:

- Good signal and 5G connectivity,
- Reset your APN settings and rebooted,
- Disabled Wi-Fi Calling,
- Enabled storage and SMS permissions for your messaging app,

and you’re still unable to send picture messages, you’ve already tried all the standard solutions for MMS issues.

At this point, your issue may require more advanced technical support. I will transfer you to a human agent who can assist you further.
